name: Our Natural World grants
summary: Rolling grants, from £30,000 and usually over three to five years, for UK organisations working to restore peatland, freshwater, land and sea for nature at scale. Capital costs are not covered, and the foundation favours systems change over single-site or single-species work.

steps: Submit an expression of interest and complete the DEI form

eligibility.rule: Having a turnover of at least £100,000 in the latest set of accounts
Has measures to guard against disproportionate personal benefit
Doing work that is charitable and for the public benefit
Not doing work primarily the responsibility of statutory authorities using public funds
Not doing academic research unless it can demonstrate practical outcomes
For nature recovery at scale, species-focused work must also help wider habitats, ecosystems or natural processes
For nature recovery at scale, no stand-alone community gardens, growing projects or small green or blue spaces

status.quote: Unless specified otherwise, we accept applications on a rolling basis with no deadlines.

applicant_types.quote: Organisations: we support constituted organisations, including charities and non-charities doing charitable work

geography.quote: Work that does not have a direct benefit in the UK

access.quote: Unless specified otherwise, we accept applications on a rolling basis with no deadlines.

window.quote: Unless specified otherwise, we accept applications on a rolling basis with no deadlines.

amount.quote: the minimum amount we offer is £30,000 and we have no maximum amount

consortium_required.quote: We do not require partnerships unless the work needs them.

effort.quote: After completing your EOI, you’ll be directed to our DEI form to answer questions about the leadership of your organisation and the communities your work supports.

eligibility.quote: Organisations with a turnover of less than £100,000 (as reflected in the latest set of accounts)
Organisations who do not have measures in place to guard against disproportionate 'personal benefit’
Work that is not legally charitable – defined as work that falls within one of 13 descriptions of charitable purposes and is for the public benefit
Work that is primarily the responsibility of statutory authorities using public funds e.g. social services
Academic research unless it can demonstrate practical outcomes
We will only support species-focused work where it also contributes to the recovery of wider habitats, ecosystems or natural processes.
We do not fund stand-alone community gardens, growing projects or small local green and blue spaces

after_award.quote: Annual progress reports, to be submitted one month before each grant payment is needed, and when the grant is finished.
